A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HiM research. All 20 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched, and v1's localized text overlap does not prevent recovery of the relevant content.

before.justification: v1 reports original ontology-classification experiments, performance over five runs, embedding analyses and training curves.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds HiT* comparisons, curvature/model-size ablations, a GPT-4o evaluation and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The backbone, projections, learnable curvature and loss equations remain unchanged. However, v3 Section 5.2 newly mentions 'variance regularization in our centripetal loss' without defining it or explaining whether it was previously used. The PDFs therefore leave a possible additional loss component unresolved.

E1.justification: The ontology datasets and SNLI training coverage are retained. Appendix A.7.1 adds explicitly binary subtype-question answering on WordNet, whereas v1 describes mixed-hop prediction as multiclass exact-hop prediction. This introduces a limited task variant within existing data coverage.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates only pretrained and fine-tuned Euclidean SentenceMamba baselines. v3 adds randomly initialized HiT*-Poincaré and HiT*-Lorentz comparisons on WordNet and DOID (Table 2), plus prompted GPT-4o (Table 6), substantially broadening comparator coverage.

E3.justification: New protocols include 16M/32M architecture comparisons at fixed curvatures -1 and -1/384, a 500-question GPT-4o evaluation using one prompt with WordNet entity context, and efficiency measurements at 128/256 tokens. Existing benchmark splits, training settings and classification metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds curvature and model-size ablations across both manifolds to examine architectural and geometric dependencies (Section 5.2), plus a sequence-length scaling analysis (Appendix A.7.2). The earlier WordNet geometry case study and training-dynamics analyses are retained, including material moved into the appendix.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains identical means and standard deviations over five independent runs, and the existing plots retain their uncertainty displays. No new seeds, run counts, confidence intervals or significance procedures are documented. The added comparison tables provide point estimates without additional uncertainty information.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the retained geometry/training results are unchanged. New Table 2 reports, for example, 16M WordNet Poincaré F1 of 0.859/0.846 for HiM/HiT* at curvature -1, but 0.788/0.840 at -1/384. Tables 6–7 add GPT-4o F1 of 0.750 and scaling measurements, including 4.46/8.90 GFLOPs at 128/256 tokens. These concern added experimental settings.

T1.justification: v3 removes v1's effective-curvature claim K_eff = -1/(c gamma^2) and its argument equating embedding scaling with changing curvature. It instead describes gamma as controlling embedding spread. The numbered equations, geometric definitions and task formulations otherwise remain materially unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims about integrating Mamba2 with hyperbolic geometry, SentenceMamba-16M and hierarchical performance remain. v3 narrows the contribution wording by removing the explicit claim that its task-specific hyperbolic losses are novel, including from the contribution list.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations attributing fixed-curvature behavior to Poincaré norm dispersion and Lorentz shell collapse, and interprets the new comparisons as supporting specialization and efficiency. It removes v1's explicit limitation that broader NLP applications, including real-time inference, remain underexplored. Earlier geometric interpretations are retained in the appendix.

D1.justification: v3 documents the GPT-4o question template and context construction and reports computation, memory and training times. Conversely, it removes the explicit margin coefficients alpha=0.255r and beta=0.0051r, retaining only proportional scaling. Core implementation settings, hardware and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Dhingra et al. (2018) and Patil et al. (2025), including discussion of earlier hyperbolic recurrent encoders. It also replaces the specific claim that Hyperbolic BERT is 1.3 times slower with a general computational-cost statement. The broader research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The abstract is condensed and selected passages, author information and acknowledgments are edited. The former Section 5.3 geometry discussion moves to Appendix A.5, and the appendices are reorganized under one hierarchy. Most existing exposition is retained.

P2.justification: v3 changes typography, text width, author layout and display sizing throughout. It relocates the geometry figure and tables into the appendix, adds Tables 2, 6 and 7, and fixes the overlapping paragraph and Table 1 caption in v1. Existing plots and diagrams are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The controlled HiT* comparisons and curvature/model-size ablations provide useful evidence beyond v1's Euclidean-only comparisons, while measured scaling results and the repaired Table 1 layout improve support and readability. The gain is limited: GPT-4o's binary-question protocol is not clearly aligned with the reported HiM scores or exact-hop formulation, variance regularization remains undefined, and explicit loss-margin coefficients and an applicability caveat disappear. Overall, the additions provide a modest net improvement.
